sermon.title: Sodom in the New Testament
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer lays out a timeline of 400-year patterns of God’s judgments, then studies the three New Testament mentions of Sodom (Mark 6, Matthew 11, Luke 17), arguing that Sodom is the example for the end times, that the apostles preached repentance, and that Lot’s wife shows the danger of going back. He closes with his view of conditions in America.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: one name in Matthew 11:20-24 is garbled in the captions (the cities Jesus rebuked) and is marked [unclear]. He gives statistics on sexually transmitted diseases, single parents, rape, suicide and unemployment, and links AIDS to homosexuality; these are his statements and are not verified here. He also names a government figure and news organizations as sources of those statistics. His views on welfare, homosexuality, same-sex marriage, and the antichrist are his own.

chunks.section_question: What is the 400-year pattern between God’s judgments?
chunks.short_answer: He lays out a timeline in which about 400 years separate the flood, the judgment of Sodom, the judgment of Egypt, the period of the judges, the era of the kings, and then 400 silent years before Jesus came. He says Jesus did not follow the pattern for His return “cuz we’re 2,000 years from that time,” but he says judgment is surely coming.

At the flood, there’s approximately 400 years between that judgment and the judgment of Sodom and Gomorrah, okay? When God destroyed Sodom, then we come over here to the Exodus. Israel was 400 years from Sodom. Abraham and had sons, and then they had sons, and they went down to Egypt for actually 430 years, but approximately 400 years between Sodom and God judging Egypt and literally destroying Egypt to set his people free. Are you with me so far?

We find that the period of the judges was approximately 400 years. Everybody doing what’s right in their own eyes. The judges were brought up to judge God’s people. he would He would bring in armies or plagues to correct God’s people, and then he would raise up a judge to lead them out of the captivity, the judgment. All right, that was 400 years, approximately 400 years. Are you getting the picture? 400 years is all of a sudden a prominent figure in God’s judgments. All right. Then we come over here to where they have a king. They didn’t want to judge anymore, and so they wanted a king. They wanted to be like the nations. And this is during the era of the kings is when God, through Jeremiah and Ezekiel, said that his people was like Sodom and Gomorrah. They were sinning. And so, sure enough, it was about 400 years of the reigns of the kings, and then God took them into captivity, the Babylonian captivity.

chunks.short_answer: He says Jesus Himself said there would be a falling away and that the second coming would be like Sodom, and that the pre-, mid- and post-tribulation and millennial views all “have a real problem, because no one is connecting it to what God said is the example of the end.” He says the next “Sodom example” comes at the return of Christ.
chunks.text: Folks, supernatural gods can predict things before they ever happen. Nobody else. But it’s also coincidental that over here, Jesus himself said there would be a falling away, and we would be like Sodom at the second coming of Jesus Christ. And this is where all your second uh return, your your end time predictions are all wrong. I’ve studied them all. They all have a problem: pre-tribulation, post-tribulation, mid-tribulation, premillennium, postmillennium, amillennium. All these things have a real problem, because no one is connecting it to what God said is the example of the end. We do all this crazy stuff with weeks and Daniel and all this nonsense, and we get God’s people all, we lead them. Okay, now we got the picture of the timeline. When’s the next next Sodom example coming? At the second coming, the return of Christ. Okay, we don’t know how long, we don’t know how many years people try to predict it, but we know that one of the signs is things are going to be like Sodom and Gomorrah. Right? Yeah. chunks.short_answer: He says Jesus sent the apostles out and said that for people who would not receive or hear them, it “shall be more tolerable” for Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city. He says this shows “there’s levels of judgment” and that those who reject the message and the preachers get a greater judgment than Sodom.

And he says whoever rejects the message and whoever rejects and mistreats the preacher preaching it, “I say it shall be more tolerable,” more bearable, it be a better word here, “for Sodom and Gomorrah in the” what? “Day of judgment than for that city.” Wow. He says what is rejected is repentance, “not grace and faith,” and that “if you don’t” stop sinning “you’re like Sodom and Gomorrah.”

chunks.text: He said, “Remember Lot’s wife.” What happened to her? She got caught in the judgment and turned to a pillar of salt, just like everything else was salt in that area, and it’s still salt. And this, he explains, “If you seek to save your life,” and that’s what she did, “I’m not going to follow them guys, I’m going to do it my way.” Isn’t that what happened in Judges? They did what was right in their own eyes. Isn’t that what happened at the flood? They did what was right in their own eyes. And that what happened, went into captivity, everybody was doing what was right in their own eyes. No repentance, no Bible morality. They all believed in God, but no Bible morality, no repentance. “And whoever loses his life,” you give up your way of doing things, “you will find it.” You will get life. Isn’t that right? You go God’s way, you’ll live. Repent, turn from your sins, accept Jesus’ sacrifice on the cross for the punishment for your sin, you will live. If you do it your way, you will die. Ain’t that clear? Did Lot’s wife die with two angels leading her out? Yeah.

chunks.section_question: What does he say sin is, and what does he say about sexual immorality and homosexuality?
chunks.short_answer: He says sin is “just a Bible word for crime,” a violation of a moral law with a punishment. He says sexual immorality is much bigger than homosexuality because more people commit it, that Sodom’s second sin was pride, “fullness of bread, abundance of idleness,” and that we are to strengthen the hand of the poor by getting them a job. He also says that AIDS is “a obvious judgment on the male homosexuals,” which is his own claim and not verified here.
chunks.text: Remember their sins. Sodom’s crimes. Sins is just a Bible word for crime. And so when you use sin, they say, “Well, we can’t use the word sin.” Sin is nothing but the same word as crime. You violated a moral law, it is a crime, there’s a punishment, there’s a hurt that’s going to be done. Are you with me? United States, in Europe today, and at the second coming. All right, sexual immorality is much bigger than homosexuality, because there’s more people committing sexual immorality than there is people committing homosexuality, and how’s he going to single out the homosexuals and just judge them, except for this AIDS thing? You know, that’s a obvious judgment on the male homosexuals, cuz, you know, 90% of the people who have it are male homosexuals, over 90%, 94 or something like that. Are you there? We need to correct our sexual immorality, also incest, adultery, fornication, sex with animals, and all that stuff. Sexual immorality, homosexuality was the second sin. Pride, of course. America has no pride. Right? Fullness of bread, abundance of idleness. Do we have abundance of idleness? We we went through all this. Yeah, we’re lining up. Boy, we’re we’re right there. We don’t strengthen the hand of the poor and the needy. And how do you strengthen the hand of the poor and the needy? Getting them a career, getting them a job, getting them work. That’s right.

chunks.section_question: What does he say the Bible calls an abomination?
chunks.short_answer: He lists sexual immorality, homosexuality, incest, pedophilia, sex with animals, witchcraft, all child abuse, desecrating God’s house, stealing and lying, and says failing to tell people to repent is also an abomination. He says an abomination is “something God detests” because it brings harm.
chunks.text: Abominations. Abominations include sexual immorality, homosexuality, incest, pedophilia, sex with children, sex with animals, witchcraft, all child abuse, including the murder of children. The Bible declares is an abomination. When you mistreat a child, whether it’s verbally, physically, sexually, emotionally or whatever, God says that’s an abomination. Not telling people to repent, we just learned, as an abomination. Okay. Desecrating God’s house is an abomination. Stealing, lying, all this stuff, that’s an abomination. Abomination is something God detests. God hates it because it brings harm. Now, they declared openly their sin. They didn’t hide it. And we just found that, as I said, no repentance to the gospel message is their sin. All right, and that’s the way it’s going to be at the coming of Christ.

chunks.section_question: Why does he say no one predicted these changes in America?
chunks.short_answer: He says that in the circles he grew up in, no one predicted laws for same-sex marriage and acceptance of homosexuality, which he says gained “inroads” in churches and politics. He says no one predicted the fall of Russia “overnight,” and that if God can bring that down He can bring down America, quoting the warning not to trust in chariots or horses.
chunks.text: Now let me just say, back in those years growing through all that, the people around me and I myself, who became a tongue-talking, spirit-filled believer, wound up in a circle of churches that believed in prophecy, setting people into the body of Christ. And nobody that I read books on, no preacher, no minister that I talked to, and no minister, big mega church on TV and radio, even gave an indication, even a thought, that America would be passing a law for same-sex marriage, homosexuality accepted, that these homosexuals would have infiltrated the churches, the politics, Congress, local city councils, mayors, state, and that one to two of people would gain inroads like they have today. No one predicted it, including us tongue talkers who supposed to be a notch above everybody else, man. You know, nobody. They were all saying, “Jesus is coming, Jesus is coming, Jesus is coming.” Oh man, no one predicted the fall of Russia overnight, just like that. And if God can bring down Russia overnight, can he bring down America? Oh yeah, he’s God, folks. That’s why the scriptures say don’t trust in chariots, don’t trust in horses. Back then, those days, that was the tremendous weapons, the cavalry, the armor was the chariots. He said, “Don’t trust in your army. When I decide to do something, armies don’t even get in my way.” Are you there?

chunks.section_question: What does he say about sexually transmitted diseases?
chunks.short_answer: He says no one predicted the sexual revolution would leave about half of Americans with a sexually transmitted disease or over 30 new ones, and he says over 30,000 Americans die of them a year. He says “if it feels good, do it” hurts others, and that accepting homosexuality sentences a man “to a horrible death of AIDS.” These statistics are as he gave them and have not been checked.
chunks.text: None of these people were predicting these things. None of these were predicting when the sexual revolution came along. No one predicted that America would wind up with 50% of Americans with a sexually transmitted disease today. 50% of Americans have a sexually transmitted disease or had one, or got more than one, one-half, one and two. No one predicted there were to be 30 over 30 and new sexually transmitted diseases. No preacher was predicting that. No politician was predicting that. Just, you know, “if it feels good, do it.” That was the statement back there. Am I right, you older ones? “If it feels good, do it. I’m not hurting anybody else.” Yeah, you do hurt somebody else when you do these things, and it starts spreading through America. Over, and about 27, 28,000 of those, those are AIDS. They die from AIDS. When you say the homosexual is acceptable and they come, you are sentencing that man to a horrible death of AIDS. Nowhere else do we sentence people to a disease. Are we like Sodom and Gomorrah? Oh yeah, oh yeah.

He also says 93,000 men and boys and 19,000 military women were raped in a year, and only 8% are punished; these figures are as he stated them and have not been checked.

chunks.section_question: What does he say about suicide, a sound mind and hope? (2 Timothy 1:7, Romans 8:24)
chunks.short_answer: He says 105 people commit suicide every day, 8 and a half of them young people, and that “Bible moral people don’t commit suicide” because God has given a spirit of power, love and a sound mind. He ends by saying “we’re saved by hope,” and that we have hope for America, our youth and our families because God is not a man that He should lie.
chunks.text: 105 people commit suicide every day. You young hearing that? 105, a lot more than all the shootings in the schools. 8 and a half of them are young people every day, young people. Eight and a half are committing suicide. You see, Bible moral people don’t commit suicide. Are you there? The Bible says he hasn’t given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of what? Sound mind, a solid mind. Sound mind people don’t commit suicide, and they don’t hurt other people. That was good. See, Christians don’t have a confused mind. We’re not confused. We have a sound mind, a solid mind, a strong mind. 49% of the unemployed are under age 34. That’s really a disaster. That’s really hurting in America, that our young people are the highest of the unemployed. Is this clear? Are we lining up to Sodom and Gomorrah? How many know the Bible says we’re saved by hope? I just gave you that verse a couple weeks ago. Hallelujah. How many Christians have never heard that verse? They always heard you say by faith through grace and not of ourselves, not a work. We saved by hope. We have great hope in his name. Amen. We have hope for America. We have hope for our youth. We have hope for our family, because God is not a man that he should lie. What he says he will do. And he uses consistent, faithful people like you to reach the inconsistent, unfaithful people that need to be reached. Amen. Hallelujah. So Bible morality preaches repentance and repents.

“God is not a man, that He should lie, Nor a son of man, that He should repent. Has He said, and will He not do? Or has He spoken, and will He not make it good?

faqs.question: What did Jesus say would be like Sodom?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus said that at the second coming of Jesus Christ “we would be like Sodom,” and that Luke 17 compares the days of the Son of Man to the days of Lot.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Likewise as it was also in the days of Lot: They ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built;

faqs.question: What does he say about end-time timelines and weeks of Daniel?
faqs.answer: He says “we do all this crazy stuff with weeks and Daniel and all this nonsense,” and that all the pre-, mid- and post-tribulation and millennial views have a problem because they do not connect to the example of Sodom.

faqs.question: Does he say there are levels of judgment?
faqs.answer: He says yes: “there’s levels of judgment,” and Sodom and Gomorrah’s people will have a lesser judgment than the people who reject the message and the preachers.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And whoever will not receive you nor hear you, when you depart from there, shake off the dust under your feet as a testimony against them. Assuredly, I say to you, it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city!”

faqs.question: What message does he say people are rejecting today?
faqs.answer: He says it is “repentance, not grace and faith,” and that “you got to turn from your sin, you got to stop sinning.”

faqs.question: Does he say Sodom was judged only for homosexuality?
faqs.answer: He says “we got to get it out of our mind that God’s just going to judge homosexuals and sexual immorality people because that’s what Sodom” was, and says Jeremiah and Ezekiel referred to God’s own people as being like Sodom when they did worse sins.

faqs.question: Does he say miracles make people repent?
faqs.answer: He says no: the cities where most of the miracles were done did not repent “even though he did all the miracles,” and he says Jesus said Sodom would have repented if it had seen them.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then He began to rebuke the cities in which most of His mighty works had been done, because they did not repent: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works which were done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes. But I say to you, it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the day of judgment than for you. And you, Capernaum, who are exalted to heaven, will be brought down to Hades; for if the mighty works which were done in you had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day. But I say to you that it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment than for you.”

faqs.question: What does he say about welfare and work?
faqs.answer: He says people who do not work still get to eat, with salary and welfare raised for more children, and compares it to Sodom, where “you didn’t even have to work. They’d feed you.” He says the way to help the poor is getting them “a career… a job.”

faqs.question: What does he say about the righteous in times of judgment?
faqs.answer: He says God “always protects the righteous,” like the remnant in Israel, and that “in the midst of this mess God makes these promises” to His people.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Yet I have reserved seven thousand in Israel, all whose knees have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth that has not kissed him.”

faqs.question: What does he say about the antichrist?
faqs.answer: He says “There ain’t no big bad uh son of perdition, the antichrist, rising up,” and that “the Bible never says that the son of perdition is the antichrist.”

faqs.question: Why does he say Lot’s wife turned to salt?
faqs.answer: He says she “got caught in the judgment and turned to a pillar of salt,” because she chose to do it her own way instead of following the angels and her righteous husband.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Remember Lot’s wife.

faqs.question: How does he define sin?
faqs.answer: He says “sin is nothing but the same word as crime,” a violation of a moral law that carries a punishment and a hurt.

faqs.question: What does he say about child abuse?
faqs.answer: He says the Bible declares all child abuse, “including the murder of children,” an abomination, whether verbal, physical, sexual or emotional.

faqs.question: What does he say about suicide?
faqs.answer: He says 105 people commit suicide every day, that “Bible moral people don’t commit suicide,” and that the Bible promises a spirit of power, love and a sound mind. Anyone struggling should reach out for help from a crisis line or a trusted person.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind.

faqs.question: What does he say we are saved by?
faqs.answer: He says “we’re saved by hope,” that many Christians have never heard that verse, and that we have great hope in His name.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For we were saved in this hope, but hope that is seen is not hope; for why does one still hope for what he sees?
